The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336095;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #336095;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336095;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7d5500;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336095;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #336095;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336095;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #90396f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6947a8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d19;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #884d19;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d19;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668c;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00668c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668c;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7d5500;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6947a8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668c;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00668c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #90396f;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306d32;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #306d32;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306d32;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d19;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #884d19;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d19;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7d5500;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00668c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6947a8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #90396f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336095;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #336095;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336095;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336095;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #336095;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336095;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d19;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #306d32;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #306d32;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #306d32;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6947a8;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #90396f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7d5500;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863599;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #863599;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863599;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6947a8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7d5500;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7d5500;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668c;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00668c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #964028;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #964028;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #964028;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6947a8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6947a8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668c;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00668c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863599;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #863599;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863599;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c67;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c67;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c67;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #90396f;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d19;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #884d19;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d19;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #863599;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #863599;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #863599;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336095;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #336095;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336095;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #90396f;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #90396f;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #90396f;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #54661a;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #54661a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #54661a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a79;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a79;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a79;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3549;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3549;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6b5e00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5e00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse; The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the table below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><p><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #884d19;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #884d19;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #884d19;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046f51;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #046f51;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046f51;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4653b3;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4653b3;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul></p><table style="border-collapse: collapse;
